BREAKTHROUGH IN BITCOIN CRYPTOGRAPHY: RESEARCHERS UNVEIL FIRST PRACTICAL WITNESS ENCRYPTION FOR GENERAL NP

Researchers at Byzantine Research and Stanford University have introduced Praxis, a new cryptographic scheme that could unlock major advances in Bitcoin scaling, trust-minimized bridges, and smart contracts.

Witness encryption allows information to be encrypted so that only someone possessing a valid mathematical proof can decrypt it.

At 100-bit security, Praxis achieves:

Ciphertext size: Under 8 GB
Encryption and decryption: Seconds
Security: Formally verified in Lean 4 under specified cryptographic assumptions

Compared with previous constructions, Praxis reduces ciphertext size and encryption costs by more than 10 orders of magnitude, and decryption costs by more than 6 orders of magnitude.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR BITCOIN:

The researchers’ primary motivation is enabling non-interactive proof verification on Bitcoin without requiring challengers or operators.

This could potentially enable:

More trust-minimized Bitcoin bridges: Reducing reliance on third-party operators and honest challengers to prevent fraudulent transactions.

Improved Bitcoin scaling: Enabling more sophisticated off-chain computation with fewer interactive verification requirements.

More powerful Bitcoin smart contracts: Opening the door to new applications and conditional execution mechanisms without necessarily requiring changes to Bitcoin’s consensus rules.

Reduced trust assumptions: Allowing certain cryptographic proofs to be used without depending on an independent party to monitor and challenge invalid claims.

The breakthrough could address one of the major limitations of existing Bitcoin scaling proposals, including BitVM-style systems that rely on interactive fraud proofs and honest challengers.

While Praxis remains an early-stage research result rather than a production-ready Bitcoin solution, it represents a significant advance toward making witness encryption practical.

Paper: https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2971

tweets.text:
The controversy surrounding Ansem brings us back to the same recurring problem in crypto: influencers using their influence to enrich themselves at the expense of their own audience.

But the problem goes much deeper than any individual.

In my opinion, crypto broke the moment anyone could create a token in minutes, manufacture a narrative around it, and monetize speculation without delivering anything of real value.

We created an ecosystem where influence became more profitable than innovation, and where extracting liquidity became more rewarding than building something meaningful.

And unfortunately, it's usually the least experienced investors and those with the least money who end up paying the price.

I also want to take this opportunity to make something clear: you will never see me putting myself in that position.

As I explained in a previous post, which I encourage you to read, from 2027 onwards, I won't even be covering altcoins or individual projects anymore.

It's a personal decision based on respect for my audience and the responsibility that comes with having a platform.

Having influence is a privilege. Exploiting it for personal financial gain at the expense of those who trust you is a choice.

Crypto has enormous potential, but until the industry stops rewarding this kind of behavior, it will continue to destroy its own credibility.

I genuinely hope things change in the future.

This industry could be so much better than what it has become.

quote.text:
Yesterday the Nasdaq 100 jumped 6.9%, its best day since April 2025. Nvidia rose 31% after Jensen Huang's return as CEO.

Bitcoin barely followed. Today it is down 2.7%, at about $59,500.

Since the Oct 6 market peak:

> Nasdaq up days: Nasdaq +1.67% on average, Bitcoin +0.65%
> Nasdaq down days: Nasdaq -1.72% on average, Bitcoin -1.94%

Bitcoin has captured 113% of tech's downside but only 39% of its upside.

Result: the Nasdaq 100 is down 14% from the peak. Bitcoin is down 28%.

Is Bitcoin a risk asset, a hedge, or neither right now?

Bitcoin barely followed. Today it is down 2.7%, at about $59,500.

Since the Oct 6 market peak:

> Nasdaq up days: Nasdaq +1.67% on average, Bitcoin +0.65%
> Nasdaq down days: Nasdaq -1.72% on average, Bitcoin -1.94%

Bitcoin has captured 113% of tech's downside but only 39% of its upside.

Result: the Nasdaq 100 is down 14% from the peak. Bitcoin is down 28%.

Is Bitcoin a risk asset, a hedge, or neither right now?

Another big headline.

Funnily enough, the TradFi pre-market and crypto price action the day before these massive headlines have been pretty indicative of whatever news has been dropping.

Could be a coincidence of course, but it has been happening a few times too many for that at this point.

Oil has been moving like that too for months. Can be up or down a lot, then a headline drops confirming whatever price action was preceding it, usually that in itself is then the reversal point and some hours or days later you get some headline completely supporting the other side.

tl;dr
Following these things have generally made you buy a lot of local tops and sell a lot of local bottoms. Because the move happened before the headline a lot of the times.

$BTC The New York Market open is coming up.

These have been brutal for BTC with it setting the high in the first 15 minutes most of the times and seeing an average decline of -1.07% during the 6.5 hours the market is open.

The past 5 trading sessions have been especially tough as you can see on the chart.

With Spot ETFs selling ~$500M a day it is easy to see where at least part of that selling pressure is coming from.

So prepare for the worst but be very much on the look out for when this changes. Any signs of relative strength (for more than just a few hours), ETF spot flows reversing and/or price not going down on bad news will be the first signs to watch out for.

Until that happens you can play it safe and remain patient with your trades.
